title: Etale locality and affine-target criterion for adequate moduli spaces
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $\mathcal Z/k$ an algebraic stack, $Y/k$ an algebraic space, and $f:\mathcal Z\to Y$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism, as in [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space]. For any jointly surjective etale family $(Y_i\to Y)$ of algebraic spaces, $f$ is an adequate moduli space if and only if each $\mathcal Z\times_Y Y_i\to Y_i$ is an adequate moduli space. Furthermore, if $Y=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is affine, $f$ is an adequate moduli space if and only if the map $C\to\Gamma(\mathcal Z,\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z})$ is an isomorphism and for every surjection $\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}$-algebras and every $b\in\Gamma(\mathcal Z,\mathcal B)$ there exist $n>0$ and $a\in\Gamma(\mathcal Z,\mathcal A)$ mapping to $b^n$. In this affine criterion the quantifier includes all quasi-coherent algebras on $\mathcal Z$, without finite-generation hypotheses. The algebras on a base-changed stack in the etale-local assertion are likewise arbitrary, not necessarily pulled back from $\mathcal Z$. Etaleness of algebraic-space maps is tested on scheme charts [def-weil-etale-morphism]; affine spectra use [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Alper arXiv:1005.2398v3, Lemma 4.1.8(3) and Definition 5.1.1 for the affine criterion; Proposition 5.2.9(1),(2) and Proposition 4.2.1(3),(4) for etale-locality (apply fpqc descent over affine pieces). Read online at https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: First suppose $Y=\operatorname{Spec}C$. If $f$ is adequate, evaluation of the structural sheaf isomorphism and the identity etale test in [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space] give the two necessary global conditions. Conversely assume those conditions. For any affine etale $W=\operatorname{Spec}D\to Y$, the stack $\mathcal Z_W$ is algebraic by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products], and the projection $q:\mathcal Z_W\to\mathcal Z$ is affine by [lem-sfb-stack-affine-algebra-direct-image]. Given any algebra surjection $\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ on $\mathcal Z_W$, its quasi-coherent direct image is a surjection on $\mathcal Z$. The natural global-section ring identifications of that node identify its given target section with a section upstairs. Apply the assumed global power-lifting property on $\mathcal Z$ to this direct-image surjection and transfer the lift back through these ring identifications. This proves all the required affine etale power tests. For the structural map, [lem-sfb-stack-flat-scalar-sections] applies because $D$ is flat over $C$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]; it identifies the structural map on $W$ with $D\to\Gamma(\mathcal Z,\mathcal O)\otimes_C D$. Tensoring the assumed $C$-algebra isomorphism makes this an isomorphism. The displayed unit formula of the comparison gives precisely the canonical structural map. For an arbitrary etale scheme $W'\to Y$, cover $W'$ by affine opens, which are affine etale over $Y$; on each of them and on their affine open overlaps the structural map is an isomorphism, its local inverses agree because they invert the same map, and since $\mathcal O_Y$ and $f_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}$ are sheaves [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra] these inverses glue to an inverse over $W'$. Thus both conditions of [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space] hold.

source.place: Alper arXiv:1005.2398v3, Definition 5.1.1, Remark 4.1.3 and Lemma 4.1.8(3); read at https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: For the forward etale-local assertion assume $f$ adequate. By [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products] and [lem-sfb-stack-etale-local-qcqs-homeomorphism], each $\mathcal Z_i=\mathcal Z\times_Y Y_i$ is algebraic and $f_i$ is qcqs. If $W\to Y_i$ is affine etale, its composite with $Y_i\to Y$ is etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. The triple definition of a $2$-fibre product identifies $(\mathcal Z_i)_W$ with $\mathcal Z_W$. Thus the power-lifting test for $f_i$ is literally one of the tests for $f$, including every algebra on this stack. By the direct-image formula in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], the structural map for $f_i$ on $W$ is likewise the structural map for $f$ on $W$. It is an isomorphism. These are both conditions in [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space].

source.place: Proposition 5.2.9(1), specialized to etale maps; proof expanded using the test-stack definition.

proof.text: Conversely assume all $f_i$ adequate. For any scheme $W$ etale over $Y$, [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] gives a jointly surjective etale cover $W\times_Y Y_i\to W$; its members are schemes because etale maps of algebraic spaces are representable by schemes in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. On each member the canonical map $\mathcal O_Y\to f_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}$ is the canonical map for $f_i$, by [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Its local inverse is unique; on each overlap the two local inverses agree because they invert the same map. The sheaf gluing axiom therefore gives an inverse over $W$. Since this works for every $W$, the structural sheaf map for $f$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.9(2), structural-sheaf descent, here by etale sheaf gluing.

proof.text: Fix an affine etale test $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\to Y$, an arbitrary surjection $\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ on $\mathcal X=\mathcal Z_W$, and $b\in\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal B)$. The stack $\mathcal X$ is algebraic and qcqs over $W$ by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products] and [lem-sfb-stack-etale-local-qcqs-homeomorphism]. The cover $W\times_Y Y_i\to W$ gives a covering sieve on the final object of the small etale site of $W$; by the definition of the generated sieve, its arrows factor through a member of that covering family. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-sieve-finite-affine-refinement] to that generated covering sieve to obtain finitely many affine etale maps $W_j=\operatorname{Spec}R_j\to W$, jointly surjective, each factoring through one $W\times_Y Y_{i(j)}$. The maps $W_j\to Y_{i(j)}$ are etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], the scheme $V=\coprod_jW_j$ is $\operatorname{Spec}S$, $S=\prod_jR_j$. Each $R_j$ is flat over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-product-flat-modules] makes $S$ flat, and the surjective spectrum map makes it faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat].

source.place: Proposition 4.2.1(4), affine fpqc reduction. Finite affine refinement is the existing finite covering-sieve lemma; the faithfully flat argument is expanded using existing algebra leaves.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-stack-flat-scalar-sections], the restrictions of $\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ to $\mathcal X_{W_j}$ are surjections of quasi-coherent algebras. Adequacy of $f_{i(j)}$ gives $n_j>0$ and a lift of $b^{n_j}$ there. Choose $N=\prod_j n_j>0$ and raise each lift to $N/n_j$. The resulting lifts of $b^N$ on the disjoint components form one section on $\mathcal X_V$; a compatible family of sections on a disjoint open covering is a section by the sheaf axiom. Write $M=\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$, $L=\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal B)$, $h:M\to L$, and $Q=L/\operatorname{im}h$ as $R$-modules. Naturality of [lem-sfb-stack-flat-scalar-sections] identifies the restricted global algebra map with $h\otimes_RS$. Hence the class of $b^N$ in $Q$ becomes zero in $Q\otimes_RS$, by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] applied to $M\to L\to Q\to0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] the map $Q\to Q\otimes_RS$ is injective. Thus $b^N\in\operatorname{im}h$, giving the required lift already on $\mathcal X$. If $W$ is empty, its test stack is empty and its section rings are zero; take $N=1$ and the zero section instead.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.1(4), flat base change and faithfully flat descent; compare Lemma 3.1.3. The cokernel argument is written out using Stacks 0765, 00DF and 05CK.

proof.text: The preceding construction applies to every affine etale $W\to Y$, every quasi-coherent algebra surjection on $\mathcal Z_W$, and every target section. Together with the structural sheaf isomorphism of step 3 and the assumed qcqs hypothesis, [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space] gives adequacy of $f$. Neither step 1 nor steps 4--5 restricted the algebras to finite type or assumed that algebras on a base change descend. This proves all quantifiers of the statement.

lean.note: The two declarations give the etale-local equivalence and the affine global-power criterion. The canonical affine structural ring map is characterized on every object by pullback of regular functions; unique scalar preimages of every compatible family express its bijectivity. The right-hand local statement existentially supplies the algebraicity witness required by the existing adequate-moduli predicate, rather than assuming it. The additional statement dependencies cite the definition owners of chartwise etaleness, schemes as algebraic spaces and joint surjectivity. The chartwise permanence theorem remains only a proof dependency, with a plain import.
